reviews.rationale: No causal evidence has been observed. The only records are a normal backend latency sample at 09:00:00Z and a gateway 5xx rate of 0.35 at 09:00:58Z; the gateway observation is a downstream symptom and the backend sample predates it without degradation, so no culprit layer or mechanism can be identified. The unfiltered query_changes scan returned no records for the supplied pack, which leaves every config-, deployment-, scaling-, or maintenance-based mechanism untested rather than refuted. All five hypotheses therefore remain open and unsupported, with no observed discriminator between them. I am reviewing the best-grounded existing candidate, backend_resource_saturation, because it is the only hypothesis with any observed service-side symptom in the allowed window; the review verdict is insufficient because the requested causal sources have not yet been inspected. The blocking checks below request the unobserved causal sources: backend and dependency metric timelines, backend logs for dependency or pool errors, and targeted change/config records for the remaining services before any finalization could be justified.

contradictions: Backend request latency is observed at 40 ms at 09:00:00Z (incident_3010-E-001), while the gateway 5xx spike occurs later at 09:00:58Z (incident_3010-E-007); the only backend symptom is a generic request-processing deadline at 09:00:58Z (incident_3010-E-006) with no named resource, pool, or dependency failure, so backend_resource_saturation has no observed mechanism.

The unfiltered query_changes scan returned no records for the supplied pack, so no config or deployment mechanism has been observed for any candidate; this is a causal evidence gap, not evidence that no change occurred.

Postgres connections were healthy at 30/100 at 09:00:46Z (incident_3010-E-005), which weighs against postgres_connection_exhaustion but does not exclude lock contention or slow queries; active-session, lock-wait, and slow-query telemetry for the window returned empty and therefore remain unknown.

requested_checks.expected_discriminator: A backend config change reducing pool size or changing timeout settings near 09:00Z, or a confirmed absence of any such change.

reviews.rationale: The best-grounded existing candidate is backend_resource_saturation, but the review verdict is insufficient. The only observations are a normal backend latency sample at 09:00:00Z (incident_3010-E-001), a gateway 5xx rate of 0.35 at 09:00:58Z (incident_3010-E-007), a generic backend request-processing deadline at the same instant (incident_3010-E-006), and healthy postgres connections at 30/100 at 09:00:46Z (incident_3010-E-005). No evidence names CPU, memory, worker, queue, pool, redis, postgres, or outbound payment behavior, so no observed mechanism supports any candidate. The unfiltered change scan returned no records, leaving every config-, deployment-, scaling-, or maintenance-based mechanism untested rather than refuted. The empty active-session result is unknown, not proof of health, so postgres lock contention and slow queries remain live alternatives. The blocking checks below request the unobserved causal sources: backend resource metrics, backend config changes, postgres sessions/health, and postgres lock waits/slow queries. I do not select any hypothesis for FINALIZE because no candidate has an observed cause discriminator.

review.rationale: The best-grounded existing candidate is backend_resource_saturation, but the review verdict is insufficient. The only observations are a normal backend latency sample at 09:00:00Z (incident_3010-E-001), a gateway 5xx rate of 0.35 at 09:00:58Z (incident_3010-E-007), a generic backend request-processing deadline at the same instant (incident_3010-E-006), and healthy postgres connections at 30/100 at 09:00:46Z (incident_3010-E-005). No evidence names CPU, memory, worker, queue, pool, redis, postgres, or outbound payment behavior, so no observed mechanism supports any candidate. The unfiltered change scan returned no records, leaving every config-, deployment-, scaling-, or maintenance-based mechanism untested rather than refuted. The empty active-session result is unknown, not proof of health, so postgres lock contention and slow queries remain live alternatives. The blocking checks below request the unobserved causal sources: backend resource metrics, backend config changes, postgres sessions/health, and postgres lock waits/slow queries. I do not select any hypothesis for FINALIZE because no candidate has an observed cause discriminator.
